llm.summary: The skill is a coherent planning aid, but it explicitly moves from planning into execution without asking the user first.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is project planning, and most content is consistent with producing a phased implementation plan; however, it also requires continuing into `attune:project-execution`, which goes beyond planning.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill says continuation is required after saving `docs/implementation-plan.md`, invokes `Skill(attune:project-execution)`, and explicitly says not to prompt for confirmation. This creates under-scoped agency at the planning-to-execution boundary.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains a single non-executable `SKILL.md`; no install scripts, binaries, hooks, or obfuscated code were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Writing an implementation plan is proportionate, but automatic transition to an execution skill may lead to workspace changes depending on the downstream skill and agent behavior.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, privilege escalation, credential handling, background worker, or long-running process is present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an Attune-style workflow that may proceed from planning into execution automatically. Use `--standalone` or explicitly ask the agent to stop after planning if you only want a plan and do not want code changes to begin.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: Artifact evidence supports the concern: the skill requires auto-invoking the execution phase after plan creation. This is disclosed, so it is not malicious, but it exceeds a normal planning-only scope.
[EA2] unexpected: Artifact evidence supports the concern: the instruction says not to prompt for confirmation before continuing. The bypass options reduce risk, but they rely on the user knowing to opt out beforehand.
